script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A beautiful day in the city. Birds chirping, children playing. MILLICENT, a mature woman, sits on a bench, staring at a picture of her deceased husband. She weeps silently.

INT. MILLICENT'S APARTMENT - DAY

Millicent, in her kitchen, drinks a glass of water. She hears a knock on the door. It's her neighbor, LUCY, a young, vibrant woman.

LUCY
(cheerfully)
Hey Millie! I was just making banana bread and thought you might like a slice.

Millicent smiles weakly, accepting the bread.

INT. MILLICENT'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Millicent and Lucy sit on the couch, watching a movie. Millicent's eyes gloss over as she thinks of her late husband.

LUCY
(concerned)
Millie, have you been okay since… you know?

Millicent looks down, hesitates.

MILLICENT
(sighs)
No, Lucy. I'm not. But I've been living with this pain for so long, I've gotten used to it.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Millicent sits alone, staring at the steaming coffee in front of her. A man, JAMES, takes a seat across from her.

JAMES
(softly)
Millicent? It's been a long time.

Millicent looks up, recognizes him. Her ex-boyfriend.

MILLICENT
(angrily)
What do you want, James?

James shifts in his seat, looks remorseful.

JAMES
I want to apologize. I know I hurt you, and I've carried that guilt with me for years.

Millicent rolls her eyes.

MILLICENT
Your apology can't change the past.

James reaches into his pocket, pulls out a letter.

JAMES
I wrote this letter years ago. I couldn't bring myself to give it to you then, but I want you to have it now.

Millicent hesitates, takes the letter.

INT. MILLICENT'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Millicent sits in her living room, holding the letter. She begins to read.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

Millicent sits on the same bench, looking at the same picture. But this time, she cries not of sadness, but of forgiveness.

INT. CHURCH - SUNDAY

Millicent and Lucy sit side by side in the pews. Millicent turns to Lucy, a smile on her face.

MILLICENT
(whispers)
Thank you for being there for me.

Lucy smiles back.

INT. MILLICENT'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Millicent sits in her living room, surrounded by the remnants of her husband's belongings. She picks up an old photograph, one she's looked at countless times. She tears it into pieces, letting go of the past.

FADE OUT.

---

END OF SCREENPLAY.
